A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work despite renaming DML to EMN and FUDA to DAMap. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification accuracy, adaptation timing, ablations, convergence analyses, and memory visualizations across four datasets.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds XGBoost results and accuracy/time comparisons with UDA methods.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.6 retain the same frozen-feature problem, network topology, impulse propagation, Gaussian memory, confidence-based prediction, and pseudo-label updates. The DML-to-EMN and FUDA-to-DAMap renamings do not change the procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same three Digits transfers, six Office-31 transfers, twelve Office-Home transfers, and two VisDA-C directions. The added comparisons use existing datasets and task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds XGBoost to the four main benchmark tables and introduces comparisons against CDAN, SHOT, and TPDS in Table 5, substantially broadening the comparator set beyond feature-mapping classifiers. Existing comparators remain; Direct is renamed w/o DA. DANN is listed in the setup but has no reported comparison result.

E3.justification: The new Table 5 extends the evaluation design to compare frozen-feature mapping with UDA methods that adapt deep features. The existing feature extractors, batch size of 64, and 16 adaptation epochs are retained. The best-result selection rule is newly disclosed, rather than established as a change to the earlier protocol; detailed settings for the new UDA comparison remain unspecified.

E4.justification: v2 Figure 3 adds an XGBoost trajectory to the analysis of accuracy over pseudo-label adaptation epochs. The Gaussian-blur/confidence ablations, network-size sensitivity analysis, and memory/activation visualizations otherwise match after relocation, including v1 Appendix F becoming v2 Section 4.3.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The method's prediction-confidence quantities do not constitute experimental uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: All original benchmark and ablation scores are retained, but XGBoost results and the UDA accuracy/time table substantially extend the evidence. For example, v2 Table 5 reports Office-Home accuracy/time of 65.5%/0.57 ms for EMN and 71.8%/81.14 ms for SHOT. These are newly reported comparisons; the different EMN accuracies in Table 5 do not establish same-setting changes to the retained benchmark results.

T1.justification: The problem definition, Gaussian assumptions, and mathematical content of Equations 1–17 are retained. The output-symbol capitalization correction in Equation 1 is not substantive. Neither version adds formal theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction replace v1's claim of more than 10% accuracy improvement and 87% timing reduction relative to MLP with up to 10% improvement at less than 1% of traditional domain-adaptation timing cost. This changes the comparator scope and substantially strengthens the headline efficiency claim, while retaining the methodological contributions.

C2.justification: v2 interprets Table 5 as showing comparable accuracy to UDA methods without heavy feature optimization. Section 4.3 also newly emphasizes that relatively high performance is reached with 50 hub/bridging nodes. Existing explanations concerning Gaussian blur, noisy pseudo-labels, memory adaptation, and potential edge deployment remain substantially unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 specifies additional comparator configurations, including BLS enhancement nodes and incremental steps, SVM kernel settings, KNN neighbors, and ensemble sizes, and discloses best-result reporting. However, it omits v1's source-training epoch counts, adaptive learning-rate description, and explicit statement that Gaussian blur was disabled for the network-size analysis. These are documentation changes, without evidence that the retained experiments were altered.

R1.justification: v2 adds the XGBoost and TPDS references and removes references including PadCLIP, generative co-training, selective pseudo-labeling, and adversarial dropout regularization. The related-work discussion and positioning of distributed memorization against function-fitting networks remain largely intact.

P1.justification: The abstract and opening motivation are rewritten, dataset and network descriptions move into Section 4.1, parameter analysis becomes Section 4.3, and the earlier appendices are reorganized under a consolidated experimental appendix. Terminology, title, and authorship also change, and an Impact Statement is added.

P2.justification: The dataset-summary table is removed, a UDA accuracy/time table is added, benchmark tables gain XGBoost rows, and the main convergence plot is redrawn. The network-size figure moves into the main text, while memory and activation figures move to enlarged appendix displays. These constitute substantial display and layout revisions despite retaining most underlying graphics.

improvement.justification: The new UDA comparisons make the accuracy–cost tradeoff against relevant adaptation methods visible, and explicit baseline configurations improve reproducibility. The gain is limited by omitted training and ablation details and insufficiently specified UDA comparison settings. The revised headline speed claim also overgeneralizes: Table 5's Digits timings are 0.37 ms for EMN versus 2.88 ms for SHOT, approximately 13% rather than less than 1%.
